{{short description|British mathematician (1862–1933)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
[[File:Leonard James Rogers.jpg|thumb|Leonard James Rogers]]
'''Leonard James Rogers''' [[Royal Society|FRS]]<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = D. | first1 = A. L. | title = Leonard James Rogers. 1862-1933 | doi = 10.1098/rsbm.1934.0013  | doi-access = free| journal = [[Obituary Notices of Fellows of the Royal Society]] | volume = 1 | issue = 3 | pages = 299–301 | year = 1934 | jstor = 768830}}</ref> (30 March 1862 &ndash; 12 September 1933) was a British [[mathematician]] who was the first to discover the [[Rogers–Ramanujan identity]] and [[Hölder's inequality]], and who introduced [[Rogers polynomials]].<ref>{{MacTutor Biography|id=Rogers_James}}</ref> The [[Rogers–Szegő polynomials]] are named after him.

==Early life and education==
Rogers was born in [[Oxford]], the second son of [[James Edwin Thorold Rogers]] and his second wife Anne Reynolds, and brother of [[Annie Rogers]].<ref name="ODNB">{{cite ODNB|id=35815|first=Anita|last=McConnell|title=Rogers, Leonard James}}</ref> He matriculated at [[Balliol College, Oxford]], graduating [[Bachelor of Arts|BA]] and [[Bachelor of Music|BMus]] in 1884 and [[Master of Arts (Oxford, Cambridge, and Dublin)|MA]] in 1887.

==Academic career==
Rogers became [[lecturer]] in mathematics at [[Wadham College, Oxford]] in 1885.<ref>{{alox2|title=Rogers, Leonard James}}</ref>

In 1888 Rogers was appointed [[Professor]] of [[Mathematics]] at the [[Yorkshire College]], by then a constituent college of the [[Victoria University (United Kingdom)|Victoria University]].  The Yorkshire College became the [[University of Leeds]] in 1904. In 1919 he retired because of poor health.<ref name="ODNB"/>

Rogers worked initially on reciprocants in the theory of [[differential invariant]]s, and then moved into the area of [[special function]]s, where he anticipated results of Ramanujan.  In the late 1920s, he published in the ''[[Mathematical Gazette]]'' four notes on geometrical problems, including on [[Malfatti circles|Malfatti's Problem]].

==Honours==
He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS) in 1924.<ref name="ODNB"/>

==Death==
Rogers died in Oxford on 12 September 1933, aged 71.<ref name="ODNB"/>
